note: A tune that leaps a 5th, learned in named stages (with the tune, Tune muted, Chords muted), then a line of the singer's own from the home chord's notes over the 1st, 6th, 4th and 5th chords, written as tokens and counted the long way. The old Key selector is now moves (any key, 60 to 90 bpm), with the line about another key marked {{?key}}; the backing track keeps its distance above the tune's tempo.

exercise.title: A tune with a 5th, then your own line
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol each belong to more than one of these four chords, so a line made from the three fits wherever it leaps.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. The tune leaps from Do up to Sol and runs back down. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once the leap lands without a slide, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, but the leap is still Do up to Sol.

cells.heading: Your line over the backing track

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together. The backing track plays {{chord:I}}, {{chord:vi}}, {{chord:IV}} and {{chord:V}}, a bar each.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, {{chord:vi}} the 6th, built on {{6}}, {{chord:IV}} the 4th, built on {{4}}, and {{chord:V}} the 5th, built on {{5}}. Make up a line from the ringed {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}}, and start each phrase with a leap. Sing it on "ah".
When a leap misses, sing only that leap again slowly, then put it back in the line.
